Good practices (industry):
Water, dust and environment:
• IP rating targeted from the concept stage (IEC #): seals, baffles and drainage paths designed
• Conformal coating on boards exposed to humidity
• Materials stable under UV, humidity and household products
• Membrane vent against condensation in a sealed enclosure
• IEC # environmental tests planned early (damp heat, cold, transport vibration)
Structure and mechanics:
• Safety factor of at least # on structural parts (# for a plastic under long-term load: creep)
• Calculation or finite-element simulation of loaded parts, including drop and impact cases
• Tolerance analysis (worst case or RSS) on every critical fit
• Fillets, no sharp corner or notch in a loaded area (stress concentration)
• Molded parts: uniform wall thickness, ribs, draft angles, material chosen with its datasheet
• Fasteners: specified torque, thread-locker or washer, metal inserts in plastic
• Stability: low center of gravity, tilt test on an inclined plane per the product standard
For any function:
• Peer design review (PDR, CDR) with this DFMEA line in front of the reviewers
• Lessons learned: DFMEA and field feedback from a similar or previous product
• Proven solution or qualified off-the-shelf part rather than a new technology, unless there is a quantified reason
• Quantified, verifiable requirement in the functional specification (CdCF) (Goldmine) for this function, with its tolerance

Industry best practices:
Thermal:
• Thermal budget calculated or simulated, junction temperature at least # °C below the component maximum
• Touched-surface temperature per IEC #-# (TS#) or IEC #-#, with margin
• Materials chosen with a thermal index (RTI, UL #B) above the temperature reached
• Thermal protection (thermistor, thermal cutoff) that puts the product in a safe state
• Reliable, repeatable thermal contact: specified paste or pad, tightening torque, flatness
• Component derating with temperature (manufacturer's curve)
Moving parts and service life:
• Service life specified in cycles, with a margin of at least # times the intended use
• Material pairs chosen against wear (plastic on metal, specified lubricant), no two identical plastics rubbing together
• Switches and buttons chosen for a known number of cycles (datasheet), with debouncing
• Adjustable friction or clamping, wear take-up provided
• No finger pinching or shearing by moving parts (IEC #-#, cl. #)

Good practices (industry):
Moving parts and lifetime:
• Lifetime specified in cycles, with a margin of at least # times the intended use
• Materials paired against wear (plastic on metal, specified lubricant), no two identical plastics rubbing together
• Switches and buttons chosen for a known number of cycles (datasheet), with debouncing
• Adjustable friction or clamping, wear take-up provided
• No finger pinching or shearing by moving parts (IEC #-#, cl. #)
For any function:
• Peer design review (PDR, CDR) with this DFMEA line in front of the reviewers
• Lessons learned: DFMEA and field feedback from a similar or previous product
• Proven solution or qualified off-the-shelf part rather than a new technology, unless there is a quantified reason
• Quantified, verifiable requirement in the functional specification (CdCF) (Goldmine) for this function, with its tolerance
